question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
When the train pulled in / at the station, it take / Joseph some time / to get off.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. at the station, it take.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence begins with the time clause "When the train pulled in at the station", which is in the Simple Past Tense ("pulled in").

• Since the main clause describes an action that happened at the same time in the past, the main verb must also be in the Simple Past Tense, not the Simple Present.

• The segment "it take" wrongly uses the base form (V1) "take" instead of the past form (V2) "took". The correct segment should read "at the station, it took".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "When the train pulled in" is correct — "pulled in" is the correct Simple Past form of the phrasal verb "pull in" (to arrive at a station).

• Option 3: "Joseph some time" is grammatically correct as the indirect object + object of the verb; it contains no error by itself.

• Option 4: "to get off" is correct — the infinitive "to get off" correctly follows the verb-object structure ("took Joseph some time to get off").

NOTE

• Rule: all clauses in a sentence describing events happening in the same time frame must maintain tense consistency, unless there is a specific reason (like reported speech or a general truth) to shift tense.

• Common SSC trap: examiners often plant a base-form verb (V1) where a past-tense verb (V2) is required, especially with irregular verbs like take-took, give-gave, go-went, see-saw.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Thyriod.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling of the word is "Thyroid" — a large endocrine gland in the neck that produces hormones regulating metabolism.

• The given word "Thyriod" transposes the letters "o" and "i" in the second syllable; the correct sequence is T-H-Y-R-O-I-D, not T-H-Y-R-I-O-D.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Disaster" — correctly spelt; a sudden event causing great damage or suffering.

• Option 3: "System" — correctly spelt; a set of connected things forming a complex whole.

• Option 4: "Distance" — correctly spelt; the amount of space between two points.

NOTE

• Other commonly confused medical/scientific spellings tested by SSC: Rhythm, Diarrhoea, Pneumonia, Bureaucracy, Hierarchy.

• Tip: when a word has an "i" and "o" adjacent to each other (like thyroid, avoid, poison), double-check the order — SSC frequently swaps these two vowels to create the incorrect option.

question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.
The government will build an amphitheatre.
option_1: An amphitheatre will be build by the government.
option_2: An amphitheatre will be built by the government.
option_3: An amphitheatre would be built by the government.
option_4: An amphitheatre be build by the government.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. An amphitheatre will be built by the government.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence "The government will build an amphitheatre" is an assertive sentence in the Simple Future Tense.

• Rule — Simple Future Tense:
◦ Active: Subject + will/shall + V1 + Object
◦ Passive: Object + will/shall + be + V3 + by + Subject

• Applying the rule: the object "an amphitheatre" becomes the subject; the auxiliary "will be" is used; the verb "build" becomes its past participle "built"; and "the government" becomes the agent with "by".
◦ Passive: An amphitheatre will be built by the government.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "will be build" wrongly uses the base form "build" instead of the past participle "built" after "be".

• Option 3 is incorrect because "would be built" changes the tense to a conditional/past-future form, which is not present in the original sentence.

• Option 4 is incorrect because "be build" omits the auxiliary "will" and again uses the wrong verb form "build" instead of "built".

NOTE

• Common irregular verb trap: build – built – built (same form for V2 and V3). Other similarly-tricky irregular verbs: send-sent-sent, spend-spent-spent, lend-lent-lent.

• Always check that the passive sentence retains the exact same auxiliary/modal ("will", "can", "must", etc.) as the active sentence.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
She acted as if she is the one who was hurt.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. as if she was.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence uses the subordinating conjunction "as if", which is used to describe a hypothetical or unreal situation, comparing it with reality.

• Rule — "as if / as though" with a past main verb: when the main clause verb is in the past tense (here, "acted"), the clause introduced by "as if" must also be in a past form (simple past / past subjunctive "were"/"was") to maintain tense harmony, describing a state simultaneous with the past action.

• Applying the rule: "acted" (past) requires "as if she was" (past form), not a present, future, or perfect form.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "as if she has been" is incorrect because the present perfect does not agree with the past tense of "acted".

• Option 2: "as if she will be" is incorrect because the future tense cannot describe a hypothetical state simultaneous with a past action.

• Option 3: "as if she would" is incorrect and grammatically incomplete — "would" here is left without a following verb, and in any case does not match the required past-simultaneous meaning.

NOTE

• In formal/traditional grammar, "as if she were" (subjunctive) is also acceptable for a clearly unreal/hypothetical present situation, but with a past main verb, standard usage prefers the simple past "was/were".

• Similar structures tested by SSC: "He talks as if he knew everything" (present main verb + past "as if" clause for something clearly untrue); "She behaved as if nothing had happened" (past main verb + past perfect for a prior hypothetical event).

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
A rolling stone gathers no moss
option_1: A person who settles for a short time and runs from place to place, enjoying his freedom
option_2: A person who does not settle anywhere for a short time, and is always searching for gold
option_3: A person who settles for a long time and leads a boring and useless life
option_4: A person who does not settle in one place for a long time, does not gain wealth, name or fame
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. A person who does not settle in one place for a long time, does not gain wealth, name or fame.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "A rolling stone gathers no moss" means a person who keeps moving from place to place, or changes jobs/activities frequently, never settles down long enough to accumulate wealth, responsibility, reputation or stability. (जो व्यक्ति बार-बार जगह बदलता है, वह स्थायी संपत्ति या प्रतिष्ठा अर्जित नहीं कर पाता)
◦ Example: He has changed five jobs in three years — truly, a rolling stone gathers no moss.

• The idiom draws on the literal image of a stone that keeps rolling and therefore never stays still long enough for moss to grow on it.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because it describes only "enjoying freedom" without mentioning the key idea of failing to accumulate wealth/stability, and wrongly limits the settling period to "a short time".

• Option 2 is incorrect because it wrongly claims the person is "searching for gold" — the idiom is not about literally seeking wealth, but about the consequence of constant movement.

• Option 3 is incorrect because it describes the opposite behaviour — someone who settles for a long time — which is not what "rolling stone" means at all.

NOTE

• Related idiom of contrasting meaning: "Grass doesn't grow under his feet" (a person who acts quickly, without delay).

• Other frequently asked nature-based idioms: "Make hay while the sun shines" (take advantage of favourable conditions), "Every cloud has a silver lining" (something good in every bad situation).

question:
Choose the most appropriate meaning of the underlined word in the given sentence.
The students have decided to conspire to steal the test papers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Plot.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "conspire" means to secretly plan with others to do something harmful or illegal. (गुप्त रूप से साजिश रचना)
◦ Example: The employees conspired to leak confidential company data.

• "Plot" carries the same core meaning — to secretly make a plan to do something wrong or illegal — making it the closest synonym among the given options.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Enact" (लागू करना): to make a law official, or to act out a scene — unrelated to secret planning.

• Option 2: "Moderate" (नियंत्रित करना): to make something less extreme or intense — does not carry the sense of secret wrongdoing.

• Option 4: "Assist" (सहायता करना): to help someone — the opposite of secretly scheming against something.

NOTE

• Synonyms of "conspire": scheme, collude, connive, plot, machinate.

• Related word: "conspiracy" (noun) — a secret plan by a group to do something unlawful.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
An eccentric manner of living
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Bohemian.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Bohemian" refers to a socially unconventional person, especially one involved in the arts, who lives and behaves in an unusual, eccentric manner without following society's normal rules. (सामाजिक रीति-रिवाजों से हटकर, अपरंपरागत जीवनशैली जीने वाला व्यक्ति)
◦ Example: After leaving her corporate job, she adopted a bohemian lifestyle, travelling and painting for a living.

• The term originally referred to Romani people believed (mistakenly) to have come from Bohemia, and later came to describe artists and writers who lived unconventional lives.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: Numismatist (सिक्कों का संग्रहकर्ता): a person who collects or studies coins and currency.

• Option 3: Gourmet (भोजन प्रेमी): a person with refined taste in food and wine.

• Option 4: Misanthrope (मानव-द्वेषी): a person who dislikes or distrusts other people in general.

NOTE

• Other commonly asked one-word substitutes for "types of people": Philatelist (stamp collector), Epicure (one who enjoys fine food/luxury), Ascetic (one who lives a simple, disciplined life avoiding pleasure), Recluse (one who lives alone, avoiding others).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.
One must aim to develop intrinsic motivation within learners for better retention of knowledge.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Extrinsic.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "intrinsic" means belonging naturally to something; forming part of its essential nature; inherent, internal. (आंतरिक/स्वाभाविक)
◦ Example: Curiosity is an intrinsic quality of a good scientist.

• "Extrinsic" means not part of the essential nature of something; coming from or existing outside; external, which is the direct opposite of "intrinsic". (बाह्य/बाहरी)
◦ Example: Extrinsic motivation, like a reward or prize, comes from outside the individual.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Elemental" means fundamental or basic in nature — this is close in meaning to "intrinsic", not its opposite.

• Option 2: "Introjected" is a psychological term meaning to unconsciously adopt the ideas/attitudes of others as one's own — it is unrelated to the intrinsic/extrinsic contrast.

• Option 4: "Inherent" is a synonym of "intrinsic" (existing as a natural/permanent quality), not its antonym.

NOTE

• The prefix "intra-/intrinsic-" relates to "within", while "extra-/extrinsic-" relates to "outside" — remembering this prefix pair helps solve many similar antonym questions.

• Other synonym-antonym pairs on this theme: innate ↔ acquired, internal ↔ external, native ↔ foreign.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
Don't pluck the flowers.
option_1: The flowers should not be pluck.
option_2: You are requested not to plucked the flowers.
option_3: I am requesting you to pluck the flowers.
option_4: Let the flowers not be plucked.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Let the flowers not be plucked.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence "Don't pluck the flowers" is a negative imperative sentence.

• Rule — Passive of a Negative Imperative Sentence:
◦ Active: Do not + V1 + Object
◦ Passive: Let + Object + not + be + V3

• Applying the rule: the object "the flowers" becomes the subject after "Let"; the verb "pluck" becomes its past participle "plucked", preceded by "not be".
◦ Passive: Let the flowers not be plucked.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because it changes the sentence into a modal-based statement ("should not be") instead of following the imperative passive rule, and also wrongly uses the base form "pluck" instead of "plucked".

• Option 2 is incorrect because it changes the meaning to a polite request and misuses "not to plucked" — an infinitive can never be followed directly by a past participle.

• Option 3 is incorrect because it completely reverses the meaning of the original prohibition, turning it into a request TO pluck the flowers.

NOTE

• Passive of a positive imperative: Active "Pluck the flowers" → Passive "Let the flowers be plucked."

• Passive of a request-imperative (with "please"): Active "Please pluck the flowers" → Passive "You are requested to pluck the flowers."

question:
The question below consists of a set of labeled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.
P. The demand for fish has increased.
Q. However, adequate fish is not available in the lake.
R. This is mainly because the migratory fish from Chindwin-Irrawaddy river system to Manipur river system have declined steadily after the barrage came up.
S. At least two lakh people are directly dependent on the lake for fishing.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. SPQR.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sentence S introduces the topic/background — that a large population (two lakh people) depends on the lake for fishing — making it the ideal opening sentence.

• Sentence P logically follows S, building on this dependence by stating that the demand for fish has increased.

• Sentence Q introduces a contrast (signalled by "However") — that despite the rising demand, adequate fish is not available, which must come right after the demand is mentioned in P.

• Sentence R explains the reason for the shortage stated in Q (signalled by "This is mainly because..."), so it must come last, directly after Q.

• This gives the coherent, logically connected order: S → P → Q → R.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 (RPSQ) is incorrect because R (the reason for the fish shortage) is placed first, before the shortage itself (Q) has even been mentioned, making the reasoning connective "This is mainly because" meaningless.

• Option 3 (QRPS) is incorrect because it opens with "However", a contrast connective, which cannot logically begin a paragraph with nothing to contrast against.

• Option 4 (RQSP) is incorrect for the same reason as Option 2 — the cause (R) is stated before the effect it explains (Q) is introduced.

NOTE

• In parajumbles, a sentence that begins with a contrast connective ("However", "But", "Yet") or a conclusion connective ("Therefore", "This is because") can never be the opening sentence.

• Look for general/introductory statements (like S here) as likely openers, and match pronouns/connectives to their logical antecedents to fix the remaining order.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word identify from the given sentence:
My pet dog can classify and identify our family friends easily and doesn't overlook anonymous and unknown ones
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. overlook.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "identify" means to recognize or establish who or what someone/something is. (पहचानना)
◦ Example: She could easily identify her old friend in the crowd.

• "Overlook" means to fail to notice or recognize something/someone, which is the direct opposite of "identify". (अनदेखा करना/नज़रअंदाज़ करना)
◦ Example: The teacher overlooked the small mistake in the essay.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "anonymous" is an adjective (meaning "of unknown identity"), not a verb, so it cannot function as the antonym of the verb "identify" in this context.

• Option 2: "spot" means to notice or recognize — this is a synonym of "identify", not its antonym.

• Option 3: "classify" means to arrange into categories — it is close in meaning to "identify" in this sentence (both relate to recognition/categorization), not opposite to it.

NOTE

• Synonyms of "identify": recognize, spot, distinguish, classify, detect.

• Antonyms of "identify": overlook, ignore, miss, disregard.

question:
Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.
One element that
P. is timing, in particular ensuring that
Q. is essential to navigating deep space
R. the time on board spacecraft is synchronised
S. with the time on the ground
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. QPRS.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The fixed opening "One element that" must be immediately followed by a clause describing what this element does — Q ("is essential to navigating deep space") — completing the relative clause grammatically ("One element that is essential to...").

• P ("is timing, in particular ensuring that") must come next, finally naming what "one element" actually is — "timing" — and opening a new noun clause with "ensuring that".

• R ("the time on board spacecraft is synchronised") logically follows P, completing the noun clause introduced by "ensuring that".

• S ("with the time on the ground") must come last, completing the meaning of "synchronised... with...".

• This gives the coherent sentence: "One element that is essential to navigating deep space is timing, in particular ensuring that the time on board spacecraft is synchronised with the time on the ground."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 (PRQS) is incorrect because it places "is timing..." (P) directly after "One element that", which is grammatically broken — the relative clause needs a verb phrase like "is essential to..." first.

• Option 2 (PSQR) is incorrect for the same reason, and additionally breaks the logical connection between "ensuring that" (end of P) and "the time on board spacecraft is synchronised" (R).

• Option 3 (RSPQ) is incorrect because it begins the sentence with "the time on board spacecraft is synchronised", which cannot directly follow "One element that" and leaves the sentence without a coherent structure.

NOTE

• In such sentence-rearrangement questions, always locate the segment that can grammatically complete the fixed opening phrase first (here, a relative clause starting with "that" needs a verb immediately after it).

• Watch for split correlative/collocational pairs like "ensuring that... is synchronised... with..." — these phrases must stay in their natural sequence.

question:
Select the most appropriate collocation to fill in the blank.
We came to _____ as we were passing through.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. say hello.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "came to say hello" is a standard, natural collocation used when someone visits briefly, typically while passing through a place, purely to greet someone.

• Rule — Collocations: certain words habitually go together in English (verb + noun/phrase combinations); native-like accuracy requires learning these fixed combinations rather than translating literally.

• The context "as we were passing through" strongly supports a brief, casual purpose for stopping by — which matches "say hello" perfectly.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "give a hand" means to help someone with a task — this does not collocate naturally with "came to... as we were passing through".

• Option 3: "slow in" is not a standard English collocation/phrase at all.

• Option 4: "take a look" means to examine or glance at something, which does not fit the context of stopping by briefly while passing through to greet someone.

NOTE

• Other common "came to + verb" collocations: "came to see you", "came to visit", "came to check in".

• SSC frequently tests fixed collocations like "make a decision", "take a break", "pay attention", "give a hand" — always match by usage/context rather than word-for-word translation.

question:
Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the following sentence.
Apparently, he seems to be an amature person, but I know that he is a disciplined and committed person when it comes to doing something seriously.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. amature.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling of the word is "amateur" — a person who engages in a pursuit without professional skill or training, or without payment.

• The given word "amature" drops the "e" before "u"; the correct sequence is A-M-A-T-E-U-R, not A-M-A-T-U-R-E.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "apparently" — correctly spelt; means "as far as one knows or can see".

• Option 3: "committed" — correctly spelt (double "m", double "t"); means dedicated to a cause or activity.

• Option 4: "disciplined" — correctly spelt; means showing controlled, orderly behaviour.

NOTE

• The word "amateur" is French in origin (from "amator", meaning "lover of"), which explains its irregular English spelling — remember it by the ending "-eur", similar to "connoisseur", "entrepreneur", and "chauffeur".

• The related adjective form is also spelt "amateurish".

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.
The money she offered him was insufficient to persuade him to sell.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Discourage.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "persuade" means to cause someone to do something through reasoning or argument; to convince. (मनाना/राज़ी करना)
◦ Example: She persuaded her father to let her study abroad.

• "Discourage" means to make someone less determined or confident about doing something; to dissuade, which is the direct opposite of "persuade". (हतोत्साहित करना)
◦ Example: The heavy rain discouraged him from going out.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Clade" (जाति-समूह): a biological group of organisms sharing a common ancestor — completely unrelated in meaning.

• Option 2: "Propagandize" (प्रचार करना): to spread information, especially biased or misleading, to promote a cause — this is close in sense to persuading, not its opposite.

• Option 4: "Influence" (प्रभावित करना): to affect someone's actions or decisions — a near synonym of "persuade", not an antonym.

NOTE

• Synonyms of "persuade": convince, induce, coax, sway, influence.

• Antonyms of "persuade": discourage, dissuade, deter, prevent.

question: Select the sentence with the appropriate use of preposition.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Children are fond of sweets.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The adjective "fond" is always followed by the preposition "of" when expressing a liking for something.

• Rule — Fixed Preposition: "fond" + "of" is a fixed collocation in English; no other preposition (to/off/with) can correctly follow "fond" with this meaning.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "fond to" is not a valid combination; "fond" never takes the preposition "to".

• Option 2 is incorrect because "fond off" is not a standard English usage — "off" is not the correct preposition to follow "fond", and is also often confused with the identically-sounding "of".

• Option 3 is incorrect because "fond with" is not a valid combination in standard English.

NOTE

• Other adjective + fixed-preposition combinations frequently tested by SSC: afraid of, proud of, capable of, tired of, ashamed of, aware of, jealous of.

• Remember: "fond" always pairs with "of", never "to/off/with/for".

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
The great director Satyajit Ray after receiving the Honorary Academic Award from Audrey Hepburn,_________in his Kolkata home.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. breathed his last.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "breathed his last" means died; took the final breath before death. (अंतिम सांस ली/मृत्यु हो गई)
◦ Example: The old soldier breathed his last surrounded by his family.

• This fits the historical/biographical context of the sentence: legendary Indian filmmaker Satyajit Ray received an Honorary Academy Award (presented via a special video message by Audrey Hepburn) shortly before his death in his Kolkata home in 1992.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "nipped in the bud" (शुरुआत में ही खत्म करना): to stop something at an early stage before it can develop — does not fit the context of a person's death.

• Option 3: "kept the ball rolling" (काम जारी रखना): to maintain the momentum of an activity or conversation — irrelevant to the context.

• Option 4: "dug the grave" (अपने पतन का कारण बनना, literally "dug his own grave"): usually used as "dug his own grave", meaning to cause one's own downfall through one's actions — does not fit the biographical context of natural death after an honour.

NOTE

• Other common death-related idioms tested by SSC: "pass away" (die, polite form), "kick the bucket" (die, informal/humorous), "go the way of all flesh" (die, formal), "meet one's maker" (die).

• Remember the context clue: idiom-fill-in-the-blank questions on SSC are often based on real biographical/historical facts — reading the surrounding context carefully often reveals the intended idiom's meaning.

question:
Fill in the blank by selecting the appropriate word from the given options that would complete the collocation.
The judge directed the advocate general to _________ an enquiry on the case.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. hold.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The standard English collocation is "hold an enquiry/inquiry", meaning to officially conduct an investigation into a matter.

• Rule — Collocations with "enquiry": in formal/legal English, "enquiry" collocates with the verb "hold" (hold an enquiry), just as it collocates with "conduct" (conduct an enquiry) — not with "make", "produce", or "get".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "make" does not collocate with "enquiry" in this formal sense; "make an enquiry" is used only informally, to mean "ask a question", not to conduct a formal investigation.

• Option 2: "produce" does not collocate with "enquiry" at all; "produce" is used with things like "evidence" or "documents".

• Option 4: "get" is too informal and does not form a standard fixed collocation with "enquiry" in this legal/administrative context.

NOTE

• Other fixed verb-noun collocations often tested by SSC: hold a meeting, conduct an investigation, pass a resolution, lodge a complaint, file a case.

• "Hold an enquiry" specifically implies an official, formal investigative process, often ordered by an authority (as here, by a judge).

question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.
"We had opened the lock." they told me.
option_1: They said that we had opened the lock.
option_2: They said to me that they have opened the lock.
option_3: They told me that they had opened the lock.
option_4: They says that we had opened the lock.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. They told me that they had opened the lock.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The reporting verb in the original sentence is "told" (with the personal object "me"), so the indirect/reported version must retain "told me", not change it to "said" or "says".

• Rule — Pronoun Change: the pronoun "we" (spoken by the original speakers, referring to themselves) changes to "they" in reported speech, since the sentence is now narrated from an outside perspective.

• Rule — Tense of Reported Speech: since the direct speech is already in the Past Perfect Tense ("had opened"), which is the backward-most tense in English, it remains unchanged in the indirect form.

• Applying these rules: They told me that they had opened the lock.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because it wrongly changes the reporting verb to "said that" (dropping "me"), even though the original clearly has "told me", and it fails to convert "we" to "they".

• Option 2 is incorrect because it wrongly changes the tense to "have opened" (present perfect) instead of retaining the past perfect "had opened".

• Option 4 is incorrect because the reporting verb "says" is in the present tense, which does not match the past-tense narration ("they told me"), and it also fails to convert "we" to "they".

NOTE

• Golden rule: "say + to + person" changes to "tell + person", and this reporting verb form must be preserved consistently between direct and indirect speech.

• The Past Perfect Tense never shifts backward further in reported speech, since it is already the most "past" of all tenses — it stays as Past Perfect.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
The property left to someone by a will
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Legacy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Legacy" means money or property left to someone in a will after the owner's death; an inheritance. (वसीयत द्वारा प्राप्त संपत्ति/विरासत)
◦ Example: She used her grandmother's legacy to start a small business.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Ledger (खाता-बही): a book or system used for keeping financial accounts/records — unrelated to inheritance.

• Option 3: Legend (किंवदंती): a traditional story from the past, or a person who is extremely famous/admired — unrelated to property.

• Option 4: Lexical (शाब्दिक): relating to the words or vocabulary of a language — unrelated in meaning.

NOTE

• Other commonly asked one-word substitutes related to property/law: "Heir" (a person legally entitled to inherit property), "Testator" (a person who has made a will), "Beneficiary" (a person who receives a benefit, especially from a will).

• Do not confuse "Legacy" with the similar-sounding "Legend" — a frequent SSC distractor pair.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

A new world research shows that the French (1)_______ large amounts of cheese and butter. Therefore, they have low levels of heart disease. The research (2)_______ that animal fat is good for human body and helps in reducing the risks of heart attack. This study was (3)_______ in 2018 in 21 low and middle income countries. However, it (4)_______ that eating moderately is the (5)_______ key in this regard.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. consume.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank requires a verb describing the general action of the French people towards "large amounts of cheese and butter" — "consume" (to eat or drink something, especially in large quantities) fits perfectly and is the standard word used for describing dietary habits in research/reports.

• The sentence reads naturally as: "the French consume large amounts of cheese and butter."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "drink" is incorrect because cheese and butter are solid/spread foods that are eaten, not drunk.

• Option 3: "gobble" is incorrect because it means to eat something hurriedly and greedily, which is too informal and inappropriate in the formal, factual tone of a research report.

• Option 4: "take" is incorrect because it is too vague and does not specifically or naturally collocate with "large amounts of cheese and butter" in formal writing; "consume" is the more precise, report-appropriate word.

NOTE

• In formal/report-style writing, "consume" is the standard word for describing quantities of food or resources used, e.g., "consume energy", "consume calories".

• Other precise verbs often confused in cloze passages: eat vs. devour vs. consume vs. ingest — increasing levels of formality/intensity.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

A new world research shows that the French (1)_______ large amounts of cheese and butter. Therefore, they have low levels of heart disease. The research (2)_______ that animal fat is good for human body and helps in reducing the risks of heart attack. This study was (3)_______ in 2018 in 21 low and middle income countries. However, it (4)_______ that eating moderately is the (5)_______ key in this regard.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. believes.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank requires a verb describing what the research suggests or holds to be true about animal fat — "believes" fits the context: "The research believes that animal fat is good for human body...", meaning the research's findings support/hold this view.

• This is a common journalistic/informal usage where a study or research is personified as "believing" or "suggesting" a conclusion based on its findings.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "accepts" does not fit naturally — "the research accepts that..." is an unusual, awkward construction not typically used to introduce a research finding.

• Option 2: "credits" is incorrect because "credits" means to attribute something to a cause, which does not fit the sense of a research finding/conclusion being introduced here.

• Option 3: "trusts" is incorrect because "trusts" implies confidence in a person or thing, which does not fit the context of a research presenting its findings.

NOTE

• Cloze passages frequently test verbs that "introduce a finding/opinion": believes, suggests, shows, indicates, finds, reveals — context and collocation with the surrounding sentence structure determine the correct choice.

• Remember: research/reports are often personified in English writing ("the study says", "the research believes") even though, strictly, it is the researchers who hold the belief.

A new world research shows that the French (1)_______ large amounts of cheese and butter. Therefore, they have low levels of heart disease. The research (2)_______ that animal fat is good for human body and helps in reducing the risks of heart attack. This study was (3)_______ in 2018 in 21 low and middle income countries. However, it (4)_______ that eating moderately is the (5)_______ key in this regard.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. conducted.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank requires a verb collocating with "study" — "conducted" is the standard collocation used for carrying out a study/research/survey.

• The sentence reads naturally as: "This study was conducted in 2018 in 21 low and middle income countries."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "directed" does not collocate with "study" in this passive sense; "directed" is used for guiding people or projects, not for carrying out a study.

• Option 2: "managed" is incorrect because it refers to overseeing or administering something on an ongoing basis, not to carrying out a research study at a point in time.

• Option 3: "supervised" is incorrect because it means to oversee the work of others, which does not fit the context of a study being carried out.

NOTE

• Standard collocations with "study/research/survey": conduct a study, carry out research, undertake a survey.

• "Conducted" is the most natural and frequently tested passive-voice collocation for research-related cloze passages in SSC exams.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

A new world research shows that the French (1)_______ large amounts of cheese and butter. Therefore, they have low levels of heart disease. The research (2)_______ that animal fat is good for human body and helps in reducing the risks of heart attack. This study was (3)_______ in 2018 in 21 low and middle income countries. However, it (4)_______ that eating moderately is the (5)_______ key in this regard.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. concluded.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank requires a verb describing the final finding/outcome of the study — "concluded" (to reach a final decision or judgment after consideration of the evidence) fits perfectly with the connector "However", which introduces the study's final, qualifying finding.

• The sentence reads naturally as: "However, it concluded that eating moderately is the... key in this regard."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "closed" is incorrect because "closed" means to shut or end something physically or formally, and does not collocate with presenting a finding/conclusion.

• Option 3: "finished" is incorrect because it simply means to complete an activity, and does not carry the sense of arriving at a reasoned judgment or finding, which "concluded" conveys.

• Option 4: "stopped" is incorrect because it means to cease an action, and does not fit the context of presenting a research finding.

NOTE

• "Conclude" has two common meanings tested by SSC: (1) to end something, and (2) to decide something after reasoning/evidence — here, the second, report-appropriate meaning is required.

• Word family: conclude (verb) → conclusion (noun) → conclusive (adjective).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

A new world research shows that the French (1)_______ large amounts of cheese and butter. Therefore, they have low levels of heart disease. The research (2)_______ that animal fat is good for human body and helps in reducing the risks of heart attack. This study was (3)_______ in 2018 in 21 low and middle income countries. However, it (4)_______ that eating moderately is the (5)_______ key in this regard.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. crucial.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank requires an adjective describing "key" — "crucial" means extremely important, essential, decisive — and the phrase "crucial key" naturally emphasizes the vital importance of eating moderately.

• The sentence reads naturally as: "...eating moderately is the crucial key in this regard."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "diligent" is incorrect because it means careful and hardworking, an adjective typically describing a person's behaviour, not an abstract noun like "key".

• Option 3: "principle" is incorrect because it is a noun (a fundamental rule or belief), not an adjective, and cannot grammatically modify "key" in this position.

• Option 4: "eminent" is incorrect because it means famous or well-respected (usually describing people), which does not fit the context of describing an important factor/key.

NOTE

• "Crucial" is commonly paired with nouns like "role", "factor", "point", "key", "decision" to emphasize importance.

• Do not confuse "principle" (a fundamental truth/rule, noun) with "principal" (most important; or the head of an institution) — a frequently tested SSC homophone pair.
